classification.difficultyReason: Translate continuity and the linear extension's intercept into two equations, solve symbolically for m and b using a≠0, and substitute the coefficients into the piecewise definition.

content.prompt:
Consider the function $z(x)$ below, where $a\ne0$.
$$z(x)=\begin{cases}x^2,&\text{for }x<a,\\mx+b,&\text{for }x\geq a.\end{cases}$$
It is known that $z(x)$ is continuous. It is also known that the line containing the right-hand branch intersects the $x$-axis at $x=\tfrac12a$. Determine $m$ and $b$ in terms of $a$ and hence write $z(x)$ in terms of $a$ alone.

answer.worked:
Continuity at $x=a$ gives
$$\begin{align*}ma+b&=a^2.\end{align*}$$
The line has an $x$-intercept at $x=\tfrac12a$, so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{ma}{2}+b&=0\\b&=-\frac{ma}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the continuity equation:
$$\begin{align*}ma-\frac{ma}{2}&=a^2\\\frac{ma}{2}&=a^2\\m&=2a\qquad(a\ne0)\\b&=-\frac{(2a)a}{2}\\b&=-a^2.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$z(x)=\begin{cases}x^2,&x<a,\\2ax-a^2,&x\geq a.\end{cases}$$
